title: The Letters of Junebug Creek
premise: Rafael Nystrom has built his career on being nobody—ghostwriting a rival's celebrated memoirs while secretly writing anonymous letters for a decade to the woman who once saved his life. When June Calloway, the letter recipient who never knew her mysterious correspondent, moves in next door to the fading town of Junebug Creek, Rafael must maintain his invisibility even as she pieces together clues to his identity. As his rival's memoir deadline collides with June's discovery of the truth, Rafael learns she has been quietly dying to meet him for years, and that his silence cost them both a decade. In the end, Rafael sacrifices the memoir contract and his anonymity in one public act, choosing love and a found family in Junebug Creek over the career that kept him hidden.
about_author: Odile Blackwood is a former small-town postmistress turned novelist who spent years reading other people's letters and swearing she'd never write her own story down. She lives near a creek she refuses to name, where she writes romances about people who are braver on paper than in person.

chapters.title: Dead Letter Office
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In a Chicago high-rise, Rafael ghostwrites the final chapters of rival Marcus Hale's memoir while a box of ten years of unsent letters sits in his closet—letters to June, the stranger who once pulled him from a flooded creek and never learned his name. Emotional beat: the weight of a hidden life.

chapters.title: The Town That Answers Back
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A memoir research trip takes him back to Junebug Creek, where the letters were always postmarked but never delivered. He tells himself it's professional. Emotional beat: the pull of a place that remembers him.

chapters.title: Next Door
chapters.summary: June's POV. June Calloway moves into the cottage beside Rafael's rental to restore her late grandmother's house, carrying her own box—every letter she ever received from an anonymous correspondent signed only 'J.C.' Emotional beat: hope she's ashamed of.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: June's POV. June meets her new neighbor, a guarded writer named Rafael, and feels an inexplicable familiarity. He deflects with dry humor while cataloging every detail of her. Emotional beat: recognition without proof.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Marcus calls demanding the memoir be finished in Junebug Creek for 'authenticity,' and Rafael realizes his rival is circling the same letters—Marcus found one and wants to claim the story as his own. Emotional beat: dread of exposure.

chapters.title: What the Creek Kept
chapters.summary: June's POV. Restoring the house, June finds her grandmother's letters to Rafael's late mother—two women who conspired for years to bring their lonely children together. Emotional beat: grief braided with wonder.

chapters.title: Ten Junes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback chapter: the flood, the rescue, the first letter he wrote and never sent, and the mother who mailed it after his death-adjacent cowardice. Emotional beat: the origin of his invisibility.

chapters.title: Porches and Proxies
chapters.summary: June's POV. June and Rafael fall into evening porch conversations; she reads him a favorite letter aloud, watching his face. He nearly confesses. Emotional beat: intimacy built on a secret.

chapters.title: Marcus in Town
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Marcus arrives, charming the town, sniffing around June's letter collection, and pressuring Rafael to hand over the 'source material.' Emotional beat: the rival weaponizes Rafael's silence.

chapters.title: The Unsent Reply
chapters.summary: June's POV. June writes her first reply to 'J.C.' in years and asks Rafael to help her word it—asking her ghost why he never came. Emotional beat: aching irony; he edits his own indictment.

chapters.title: Found Family, Small Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A storm knocks out power; the town gathers at June's house, and Rafael is folded into casseroles, card games, and belonging he's never had. Emotional beat: the life he could have.

chapters.title: The Deadline and the Doctor
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals her heart condition and the surgery she's been postponing until she finds her correspondent—'I want to know who loved me before I go under.' Emotional beat: time is running out.

chapters.title: Stolen Pages
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Marcus steals June's letters from her grandmother's house, planning to publish them as his own romance subplot. Rafael must choose: protect the manuscript or expose his ghostwriting to stop him. Emotional beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: June's POV. On the creek bank, June almost kisses Rafael; he pulls back, and she reads the withdrawal as rejection. Emotional beat: heartbreak mistaken for indifference.

chapters.title: Confession in Draft
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael writes the truest letter of his life, then burns it, and instead confronts Marcus with a demand: return the letters or he walks. Marcus reveals he'll out him as the ghost either way. Emotional beat: nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: June's POV. At the town's summer festival, Marcus reads 'his' memoir excerpt—June's own letters in another man's voice. June recognizes every sentence and realizes her ghost has been beside her for weeks. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation at once.

chapters.title: Junebug Creek Speaks
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael takes the stage, confesses he wrote every word, every letter, for ten years, and names himself to June in front of the town that adopted him. Emotional beat: the climax—visibility at last.

chapters.title: What You Cost Me
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, furious and shattered, refuses his apology: 'You had ten years and I had one surgery.' She schedules the operation. Emotional beat: love isn't enough without trust yet.

chapters.title: The Long Recovery
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael tears up the memoir contract, publishes his own book of the real letters under his own name, and waits outside the hospital every day of her recovery—present, visible, patient. Emotional beat: atonement through presence.

chapters.title: First Delivered Letter
chapters.summary: June's POV. Waking from surgery, June finds Rafael's first letter ever delivered by hand—signed Rafael Nystrom, with the creek pebble from the day they met. Emotional beat: the circle closes.

chapters.title: The House on the Creek
chapters.summary: June's POV. Summer's end: the restored house, a porch built for two, Marcus disgraced, and the town teasing them about the letters. June writes a new letter—to their future selves. Emotional beat: joy earned, not given.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Signed in Full
chapters.summary: Both POVs, braided. One year later, Rafael reads aloud at the town library from a book titled The Letters of Junebug Creek, and June corrects his ending from the front row—'You left out the part where she forgave him.' Emotional beat: no more ghosts, only names.
